name: sudo
summary: Runs a command with another user’s privileges, root by default.
description: Superuser do: runs the command that follows with administrator privileges, after asking for YOUR password (not root’s). The right to use sudo is set in /etc/sudoers, often through the sudo or wheel group. The password is remembered for a few minutes. Every use is logged.

options.description: Runs the command as this user instead of root.
Opens a full root login shell (root’s environment).
Opens a root shell while keeping the current environment.
Lists the commands you are allowed to run.
Forgets the remembered password: it will be asked for next time.
Runs the command with this primary group.

arguments.name: COMMAND
arguments.description: Command to run with elevated privileges, followed by its own options.

examples.explanation: Updates the package list, which requires root privileges.
Opens psql as the postgres user.
Opens a root shell; type exit to come back.
Checks what you are allowed to do with sudo.
Writes to a protected file: “sudo echo … >> /etc/hosts” would fail, because the redirection is done by your shell, without privileges.

dangerNote: With sudo, a command can change or delete anything on the system. Reread the command before pressing Enter, and never run a script you do not understand with sudo.
